local({
  wave <- as.character(.wave)
  mid_band <- c(11.5, 14, 16.5, 18.5)
  band_2019 <- if_else(wave == "2019", na_if(as.numeric(B01003_2019), 9), NA_real_)
  born <- if_else(wave == "2019", as.numeric(B01005), NA_real_)
  born[!born %in% 2000:2008] <- NA
  month <- if_else(wave == "2019", as.numeric(B01004), NA_real_)
  month[!month %in% 1:12] <- NA
  derived <- 2019 - born - if_else(is.na(month), 0.5, as.numeric(month >= 7))
  lower <- recode_values(band_2019, 1 ~ -Inf, 2 ~ 13, 3 ~ 16, 4 ~ 18, default = -Inf)
  upper <- recode_values(band_2019, 1 ~ 12, 2 ~ 15, 3 ~ 17, 4 ~ Inf, default = Inf)
  age_2019 <- coalesce(pmin(pmax(derived, lower), upper), mid_band[band_2019])
  age <- case_when(
    wave == "2009" ~ as.numeric(B01P03) + 10,
    wave == "2012" ~ as.numeric(B01003_2012) + 10,
    wave %in% c("2015_sample_1", "2015_sample_2") ~ as.numeric(VB01003),
    wave == "2019" ~ age_2019,
    wave == "2024" ~ mid_band[match(as.numeric(IDADE_AGREG), 1:4)]
  )
  pmin(age, 19)
})
notes: Self-reported age, harmonised differently by edition. 2009, 2012 and 2015 ask age in single years (2009/2012 as codes 1-9 for 11 to 19; 2015 stores the age itself), with 11 meaning 11 or younger and 19 meaning 19 or older. 2019 releases only age bands (<13, 13-15, 16-17, 18+) but also birth year and month, so age is taken at 1 July 2019 (the middle of the April-September fieldwork) and clamped into the reported band; students with a birthday between April and September can be one year out, and a missing birth month counts as half a year. 2024 releases only the same four bands (IDADE_AGREG), so its ages are band midpoints over completed years (11.5, 14, 16.5, 18.5) and carry no within-band information. Partial because of 2019 and 2024; the other editions are exact. Capped at 19 (the schema maximum).

local({
  car <- coalesce(as.numeric(B01P22), as.numeric(B01017), as.numeric(VB01017))
  computer <- coalesce(as.numeric(B01P20), as.numeric(B01015), as.numeric(VB01015A), as.numeric(B01015B))
  internet <- coalesce(as.numeric(B01P21), as.numeric(B01016), as.numeric(VB01016))
  maid <- coalesce(as.numeric(B01P26), as.numeric(B01020), as.numeric(VB01020A), as.numeric(B01020A))
  car <- if_else(car %in% 1:2, as.numeric(car == 1), NA_real_)
  computer <- if_else(computer %in% 1:2, as.numeric(computer == 1), NA_real_)
  internet <- if_else(internet %in% 1:2, as.numeric(internet == 1), NA_real_)
  maid <- if_else(maid %in% 1:2, as.numeric(maid == 1), NA_real_)
  bathrooms <- coalesce(as.numeric(B01P25), as.numeric(B01019), as.numeric(VB01019), as.numeric(B01019A))
  bathrooms <- if_else(bathrooms %in% 1:5, as.numeric(bathrooms >= 3), NA_real_)
  assets <- car + computer + internet + maid + bathrooms
  ridit <- stats::ave(assets, as.character(.wave), FUN = function(x) {
    (rank(x, na.last = "keep") - 0.5) / sum(!is.na(x))
  })
  case_when(is.na(ridit) ~ "Unknown", ridit < 0.4 ~ "Low", ridit <= 0.6 ~ "Medium", .default = "High")
})
notes: PeNSE has no income or occupation item, so household SES is a count of five possessions asked in every edition in Criterio Brasil style: a car in the household, a computer at home, internet at home (2009: a home computer connected to the internet), a paid domestic worker (five or more days a week in 2009 and 2012, three or more from 2015), and two or more bathrooms with a shower. The 0-5 count is ridit-scored within each edition, as BPIPD-1528 does for the FAS, so the drift in ownership over 15 years (home computers and internet) does not move whole editions between levels; ridit < 0.4 Low, 0.4-0.6 Medium, above 0.6 High. The count has only six levels, so the bands are lumpy rather than exact quintiles. Proximate because it is a study-built asset index rather than a validated scale; any unanswered item makes the student Unknown.
